channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Kevin Warsh isn't expected to say much in Sintra: That's exactly why markets will listen
item.description: Financial markets could find an important catalyst in the enchanting, fairytale-like landscape of Sintra this week. The European Central Bank (ECB) Forum will, as it does every year, gather the crème de la crème of central banks.

item.title: US Dollar: Cyclical drivers and de-dollarisation – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley examines structural de-dollarisation themes alongside near-term Dollar dynamics. The de-dollarisation debate intensified after tariffs failed to trigger a traditional safe-haven bid for the Dollar and Treasuries in April 2025.

item.title: Euro: Sintra seasonality points to tactical strength against US Dollar – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights a recurring post-Sintra pattern in the Euro, with hawkish ECB communication from Christine Lagarde typically driving EUR/USD gains from late June into early July before they fade.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Downtrend tests 2024 low against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that USD/JPY has broken out of a brief consolidation and is now challenging its 2024 peak near 162.00. The bank notes strong May retail sales support expectations for further Bank of Japan tightening.

item.title: Eurozone: Heatwaves add macro risk for growth – ING
item.description: ING’s Global Head of Macro Carsten Brzeski warns that recurring European heatwaves are becoming a structural drag on Eurozone growth. He cites academic and ECB research showing measurable losses in output and higher food inflation linked to extreme temperatures.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Fed hikes repriced on softer inflation – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research notes that investors reduced expectations for further Fed rate hikes after softer US PCE inflation, pulling December hike pricing down and lowering 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields.

item.title: Euro: Cyclical Dollar strength versus EUR risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/USD within a broader reassessment of Dollar drivers. Foley notes that even if the US Dollar (USD) is in long-term decline, cyclical forces can still support it.

item.title: British Pound gains as UK Burnham pledges continuation of current Labour policy
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) outperforms its major currency peers, trading 0.25% higher to near 1.3230 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: Oil: Gulf de-escalation keeps crude supported – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that the U.S. and Iran have agreed to halt mutual attacks and resume talks on the Strait of Hormuz, allowing shipping to move more freely. Markets reacted cautiously, with Brent, WTI and Omani crude prices higher as tensions eased.

item.title: WTI Oi's decline stalls near $70.00 as the situation in the Strait of Hormuz muddies
item.description: Crude Oil prices are practically flat on Monday, with the price of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel practically flat around the $70.00 level.

item.title: Euro area: Oil-driven inflation relief but ECB wary – Commerzbank
item.description: Guntermann at Commerzbank notes that while Oil prices near pre-war levels reduce tail risks for growth, inflation and rate volatility, Euro area inflation is not falling fast enough to dispel European Central Bank (ECB) hawkishness.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed-driven strength and revised path – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that a more hawkish Federal Reserve and flatter US yield curve have replaced high Oil prices as the main support for the Dollar.

item.title: UK’s Burnham promises of Labour’s policy continuation
item.description: United Kingdom (UK) Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham has stated during the European trading session on Monday that his plans after getting the leadership position would be consistent with Labour’s 2024 manifesto.

item.title: Gold: Central bank flows and real yields – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem examine World Gold Council (WGC) survey data and market flows to gauge central bank demand for Gold.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains calm as investors await US-Iran talks in Oman
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades flat against the US Dollar (USD) after a long weekend on Monday.

item.title: CEE FX: Pressure returns with stronger Dollar – ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky notes that a stronger Dollar and lower Oil have led markets to outprice most rate hikes in Poland and the Czech Republic, adding pressure on regional FX.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecasts: Struggling to regain 1.1400 amid geopolitical uncertainty
item.description: The Euro (EUR) ticks higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday but is struggling to confirm a move above 1.1400, with the 13-month low in the 1.1320 area still within relatively close reach.

item.title: Euro: Shifts from selloff to consolidation against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang reports EUR/USD briefly spiked to 1.1434 before retreating, leaving intraday momentum subdued and the pair expected to trade between 1.1360 and 1.1410.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Data and BoJ Tankan to guide policy – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research points to a busy week for Japan, with strong May retail sales already released and industrial production data due.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.18 per troy ounce, down 1.63% from the $59.14 it cost on Friday.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Might correct further to near 1.4140 as oscillators start cooling down
item.description: The USD/CAD pair trades flat at around 1.14195 during the European trading session on Monday. The Loonie pair consolidates as investors shift focus to the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for June, which will be released on Thursday.

item.title: Gold weakens on US-Iran de-escalation, expectations of Fed tightening
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades around $4,050 at the time of writing on Monday, down 0.96% on the day, as investors slightly reduce their exposure to safe-haven assets following the latest developments surrounding tensions between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Gold: Shallow rallies in two-way trading – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong argue Gold may struggle to attract a clear haven bid despite renewed US–Iran tensions, as markets focus more on Oil shock risks, Dollar rebound and broader de-risking.

item.title: Iran and Oman say they hold sovereignty over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi has stated in a post on X, formerly known as Twitter, that Tehran has concluded a meeting with Oman in which review current issues related to the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint to almost 20% of global energy supply.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Policy divergence supports stronger outlook – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the US Dollar index (DXY) is trading just below year-to-date highs, with the US Dollar posting a second straight week of gains after the Fed’s hawkish update.

item.title: Australian Dollar struggles against softer US Dollar amid geopolitical uncertainty
item.description: AUD/USD remains subdued for the second successive day, trading around 0.6890 during the European hours on Monday. The pair is consolidating its recent losses as a subdued Australian Dollar (AUD) battles a softer US Dollar (USD) amid persistent geopolitical uncertainty.

item.title: Euro: Sintra tone and CPI support gains against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole expects the European Central Bank’s Sintra forum to maintain a broadly hawkish stance, with President Lagarde unlikely to signal a dovish shift ahead of June CPI.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Consolidates after sharp fall against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes AUD/USD remains locked in a short-term range between 0.6880 and 0.6920 after a recent impulsive decline. Downward momentum is starting to ease, with a break above 0.6940 seen as signalling that the major 0.6835 support is out of reach.

item.title: Brent Oil: Conflict risks ease but remain – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research’s Jim Reid and team highlight that Brent Oil fell sharply last week as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased, easing inflation concerns and rate-hike fears.

item.title: ECB: Sintra signals and sticky hike premium – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Guntermann highlights the Sintra forum as a key event for European Central Bank (ECB) communication, with Lagarde’s opening speech and a heavyweight policy panel midweek.
